cards.b: The roti you eat does not directly power your muscles. Cells first burn glucose step by step and capture the energy in ATP. Understanding this explains breathing, why exercise makes you pant, why yeast makes dough rise and how some poisons like cyanide kill so fast.

C6H12O6 + 6 O2 gives 6 CO2 + 6 H2O + energy (about 30-32 ATP per glucose). It is the reverse bookkeeping of photosynthesis. It runs in four steps and burns glucose slowly, so energy is not wasted as one big flame.

Glycolysis splits glucose (6 carbons) into two pyruvate (3 carbons). It needs no oxygen, happens in the cytoplasm and nets 2 ATP and 2 NADH. It is probably the oldest pathway, found in nearly all life. Worked out by Embden, Meyerhof and Parnas in the 1930s.

Hans Krebs described it in 1937 (Nobel 1953). Acetyl-CoA joins a four-carbon molecule to form citrate, which is stripped of carbons step by step, releasing CO2. Each turn yields NADH, FADH2 and a little ATP. The carbons you breathe out come from here.

NADH and FADH2 hand electrons to protein complexes in the inner mitochondrial membrane. This pumps protons across, building a gradient. Protons flow back through ATP synthase, making most of the ATP (chemiosmosis, Peter Mitchell, 1961). Oxygen is the final electron acceptor and becomes water.

When oxygen is short, cells keep glycolysis going by recycling NADH. Muscles make lactic acid. Yeast makes ethanol and CO2, which makes bread rise and brews beer. Fermentation gives only 2 ATP per glucose.

Antoine Lavoisier (1780s) showed respiration is slow combustion by measuring heat and CO2. Louis Pasteur showed yeast ferments without air. Mitchell's chemiosmotic idea was doubted at first but proved right.

Fix these

  • Breathing is not the same as cellular respiration; breathing supplies the O2.
  • Plants respire too.
  • Cramps are not caused only by lactic acid; the story is more complex.

Idli, dosa, dhokla, jalebi batter and toddy use microbial fermentation. Cyanide and carbon monoxide block the electron chain, which is why they are deadly. Yoga and high-altitude adaptation among Himalayan communities are studied for efficient oxygen use.

• Glycolysis, Krebs cycle and electron transport turn glucose into ATP.
  • Most ATP comes from the proton gradient.
  • No oxygen leads to fermentation and 2 ATP.

Think about it:

  1. Why does cyanide stop all ATP production?
  2. Why does a sprinter breathe hard after the race ends?
